promotionalText: Set a file-size budget, build responsive image packs and save your workflow. Native Mac image conversion, with live previews and entirely local processing.
description:
The Transmogrifier turns a folder of images into files ready to publish. Convert, resize and optimize on your Mac, with a live preview and settings you can use again.

EXPORT WITH INTENTION
• Convert common image formats to WebP, JPG or PNG.
• Set quality directly, or choose a file-size budget and minimum quality.
• Build responsive WebP packs at multiple widths, with optional JPG fallbacks and copyable srcset values.
• Resize while preserving aspect ratio, with an option to prevent upscaling.

SEE THE RESULT BEFORE YOU EXPORT
Compare the original and encoded image with a comparison wipe, shared zoom, 100% inspection and transparency backgrounds. Preview sizes reflect the encoded output.

MAKE GOOD SETTINGS REPEATABLE
Save presets for each client, project or destination. Choose an output folder, control filenames and decide how to handle existing files. Search your batch history, reveal exported files, reuse a job's settings or retry unfinished work.

MADE FOR YOUR MAC
Drag in images or folders, add files with Command-O and export with Command-Return. Optionally convert files from Finder or the Dock using a saved preset. Native SwiftUI and Core Image keep the workflow close to home.

Supported inputs include JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, TIFF, BMP, GIF, ICNS and ICO. Animated inputs are processed as still images.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
All image processing happens locally. No uploads, tracking or account required. Your images stay on your Mac.

One-time purchase. No subscription. Free updates within v1.x. Requires macOS 12 or later. Supports Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.
whatsNew:
Version 1.2.0 brings repeatable export workflows to your Mac.

• File-size budgets: choose a limit for each output and a minimum quality. If the target cannot be met, the app reports it without writing an oversized file.
• Responsive image packs: export several WebP widths, add optional JPG fallbacks and copy srcset values.
• Live comparison: inspect accurate encoded sizes with a comparison wipe, shared zoom, 100% view and transparency backgrounds.
• Better batch history: search jobs, reveal outputs, reuse settings, run again or retry unfinished variants. Completed work remains recorded when you cancel.
• A more compact workspace, direct quality controls, clearer output destinations and keyboard shortcuts.
• Optional saved-preset conversion from Finder or the Dock.

This update also improves image orientation, prevents unwanted upscaling, handles filename collisions more reliably and fixes preview caching and stale results. Existing presets and earlier conversion history remain available.
reviewNotes:
Version 1.2.0 (build 6) is a native, offline macOS image converter. No account or sign-in is required.

To test: use Command-O or drag a JPG/PNG image into the app. Choose WebP, JPG or PNG output, select an output folder with the system folder picker, then export with Command-Return. The preview updates automatically. Responsive Packs produces multiple image widths; File Size Budget attempts to meet the selected per-output limit and reports targets that cannot be reached. Batch History supports reusing settings and retrying unfinished work.

The app is sandboxed. It uses user-selected file read/write access for files and output folders chosen by the user, and app-scoped security bookmarks to retain access for saved presets and batch-history actions. It does not request broad Downloads or Pictures folder access. All image processing is local; the app has no tracking or image-upload service. Any optional conversion from Finder or the Dock uses a preset explicitly selected by the user. No special hardware is required. All features are included in the purchase.
